title: Rec Commission rename sparks the sharpest floor fight in months
blurb: Also: a data center ban advances, a new Saccarappa Park deal, Halloween road closure, and several quieter items passed without debate.
hotNote: Feisty

title: Social media attack on student athletes draws unified community response
blurb: Also: the Support Staff contract is ratified, a $38,650 emergency fire-alarm repair is approved, and a $3–6 million Siemens energy study moves forward after heavy scrutiny.

title: Stroudwater Meadows access road draws sharp opposition from nine speakers
blurb: The board also recommended the City's new data-center ban and continued two Rock Row applications for further design work.
hotNote: Stroudwater Meadows — 9 speakers, sharp access-road opposition

title: Council confirms Bruno Inácio as Finance Director
blurb: Also: a portable traffic-signal purchase projected to save about $15,000 a year in flagger wages, and renewed General Assistance ordinance maximums.

title: Committee of the Whole advances the latest boards-and-committees ordinance review
blurb: The amendment, including a one-year report-back commitment, heads to the full Council for adoption.

title: Low-attendance special meeting fills three staffing vacancies, including a one-year special-ed director role
blurb: Four of seven members present approved an interim assistant principal, a one-year assistant director of special services, and an occupational therapist, all without debate.

title: Public-comment rule change splits Council 4–2 over ward disclosure
blurb: Dropping the requirement to state your ward or address before speaking passed over objections from Councilors Chau and McCambridge.
hotNote: Ward-disclosure amendment, 4–2 split (McCambridge, Chau opposed)

title: Committee of the Whole refers four boards-and-committees amendments to Council
blurb: The Board of Assessment Review, Woodlawn Cemetery Trustees, Fair Hearing Authority, and Library Advisory Committee amendments move forward for adoption.

title: Council approves a new police collective bargaining agreement
blurb: Also: a positive update on the Student Transit Pass Program and several routine grants and equipment purchases.

title: Planning Board backs removing data centers from Rock Row's zoning
blurb: The board also approved a three-lot Longfellow Street subdivision and previewed a new "social engagement" design ordinance.

title: Chair pushes back after a board member criticizes teachers' classroom wish lists on Facebook
blurb: Also: 19 teacher/administrator hires are approved, and the high school rolls out Yonder pouches and Metro bus passes for the new school year.
hotNote: No split vote, but sustained board conflict over a member's Facebook criticism of teachers' donation wish lists

title: Planning Board approves three development extensions and site plans, all unanimous
blurb: Workshops previewed a Larrabee Road parking expansion, a reimagined Conant Street project, and a new Longfellow Street subdivision.

title: Transit-pass program passes 5–2 after an hours-long debate over a disputed bus route
blurb: An amendment to send the Monroe Avenue route change to committee failed 2–5; a separate Riverwalk North project drew long-standing abutter opposition.
hotNote: Hours-long transit-pass debate (2–5 failed amendment, 5–2 final) + Riverwalk North abutter opposition

title: High school moves to a principal/two-assistant-principal structure after seven years of co-principals
blurb: Also: Greater Portland Metro will provide free bus passes to high school students, and three administrator nominations are approved unanimously.

title: Student Transit Pass Program passes 6–1 after extended debate
blurb: Free Metro bus passes for Westbrook High School students drew concerns over cost, safety, and a new Monroe Avenue stop.
hotNote: Student Transit Pass Program, 6–1 split

title: Committee of the Whole opens review of the City's boards and committees
blurb: A proposal to drop ward-specific seats drew pushback over representation for Westbrook's poorer wards; no vote was taken.

title: Millbrook Estates affordable housing wins final approval, 3–1
blurb: Chair McWilliams dissented on design grounds; the board also workshopped a Bill Dodge Kia renovation and two Rock Row buildings.
hotNote: Millbrook Estates final vote, 3–1 split (McWilliams dissent)

title: Council previews a free student transit-pass program and a boards-and-committees ordinance overhaul
blurb: Millbrook Estates' TIF items passed with no public comment, and a sewer repair item passed after a grease-trap enforcement discussion.

title: Planning Board hears early plans for the former Twin Falls golf course
blurb: A 228-unit redevelopment across seven buildings drew only two remote comments; a routine site-plan extension also passed unanimously.

title: Tennis court repair item splits Council 5–1 amid Millbrook Estates TIF pushback
blurb: Eleven new-business orders moved forward, most unanimously, alongside a Juneteenth proclamation and a residential-growth-trends presentation.
hotNote: Tennis-court item 5–1 split + Millbrook Estates TIF public pushback

title: FY27 school budget passes with 70% voter approval and unusually high turnout
blurb: Also: Teachers of the Year and retirees with 211 combined years of service are honored, and a one-year restructuring of special-education leadership is proposed.

title: Millbrook Estates affordable housing draws sharp criticism at marathon meeting
blurb: The board also approved three other projects and workshopped a new Element by Marriott hotel at Rock Row.
hotNote: Millbrook Estates sharp criticism + 955 Bridgton Rd opposition, marathon 3.5-hr meeting

title: Council passes a Data Center Moratorium Ordinance
blurb: The meeting also paid tribute to retiring City Administrator Jerry Bryant and referred data-center zoning rules to the Planning Board.

title: Planning Board previews Rock Row's first Phase 3 buildings
blurb: A 7-story parking garage with ground-floor retail and a 6-story, ~276-unit residential building got generally positive early feedback.

title: Fire Chief previews new opioid-overdose EMS pilot program
blurb: Also: a Memorial Day parade permit, an overnight water-utility street closure, and Westbrook Together Days road closures.

title: Cell-phone ban and Yonder pouch funding both pass 5–1, Poitras dissenting on safety grounds
blurb: Also: seven retirements are announced and the district reports the FY27 budget cleared City Council and heads to referendum.
hotNote: Split 5–1 votes on cell-phone ban policy (JICJ) and Yonder pouch funding, both Poitras dissenting on safety

title: Stroudwater Meadows housing project draws heavy traffic opposition
blurb: Three large residential projects were workshopped in one unusually packed meeting; two more items ran out of time.
hotNote: Stroudwater Meadows — ~14 speakers, extensive traffic opposition

title: Rooster ban passes 5–1 after dueling public comment
blurb: The FY2026–27 budget then passed unanimously, a reversal from the first reading's 5–1 split.
hotNote: Rooster ordinance 5–1 split (Turcotte) ×2 + heated school-budget public comment

title: Revised FY27 budget gets final approval as City Council votes the same evening
blurb: A brief special meeting finalizes the $136,295.39 reduction tied to the School Resource Officer cost shift, with no discussion.

title: School budget shrinks by $136,295 as City agrees to absorb full cost of School Resource Officers
blurb: A brief special meeting adjusts three budget warrant articles after City Council moved the SRO program into the public safety budget.

title: FY2026–27 budget passes first reading, 5–1, with Rairdon dissenting
blurb: The Council also advanced several paving and infrastructure bid awards and entered executive session on a legal matter.
hotNote: Budget first reading, 5–1 split (Rairdon), sharp public pushback

title: FY27 budget adopted as teachers plead to save two cut instructional-coach positions
blurb: Also: Chair Mancuso speaks in her individual capacity against a proposed state bill on school sports and gender identity.

title: FY27 budget clears first reading at 7.5%, down from the original 9.88% proposal
blurb: Also: three staff retirements are announced and Mayor Morse voices confidence in the Council's continued full support for the school budget.

title: Finance Subcommittee locks in a 7.5% budget increase after a surprise health-insurance windfall
blurb: Also: the Chair confirms a formal request asking the City to absorb School Resource Officer costs entirely.

title: Planning Board approves 11-unit Pierce Street project, 4–1, over drainage concerns
blurb: The board also approved the Redeemer Church relocation and got its first look at Rock Row's Phase 3 master plan.
hotNote: 4–1 split vote

title: Firefighters' union challenges Chief Sloan on staffing at budget address
blurb: The Mayor delivered the FY2026–27 budget address, and the Council tabled a rooster-ban ordinance over a drafting ambiguity.
hotNote: Firefighters' union vs. Chief Sloan on staffing (no vote)

title: Finance Subcommittee cuts an English teacher and a multilingual coach as members say the City isn't carrying its share
blurb: Also: professional development and supply cuts are rejected and restored in full after real pushback.
hotNote: Sharp City-funding-fairness exchange; English teacher & Tier 2 cuts contested

title: Finance Chair says she's “not comfortable” with a 9.88% increase, orders more cuts
blurb: Also: $23,000 is added to fix the middle-school bathroom locks, and a newly disclosed data breach sharpens the case for a cybersecurity hire.
hotNote: Chair: “not comfortable with a 9.88 percent” increase, orders more cuts; ongoing City-charge frustration; Compass relocation process criticism

title: “I will have a hard time supporting this budget” — Chair presses on middle-school bathroom privacy
blurb: Also: a new committee member challenges School Resource Officer funding, and the district again presses the City on its $121,000 field-maintenance charge.
hotNote: Middle school bathroom-privacy fix (“I will have a hard time supporting this budget”), SRO funding challenged, $121K city field charge pushback

title: Finance Subcommittee digs into a special-education funding mechanism that “broke my brain”
blurb: Also: the multilingual program serves the third-largest population in Maine, and consumable-supply prices are spiking districtwide.

title: Finance Subcommittee's first budget-review night zeroes in on a $121,000 city field-maintenance charge
blurb: Also: a cybersecurity hire is requested to end the district's “single point of failure,” and new pottery wheels are sought for a booming ceramics program.

title: Council marks Finance Director Tressina Germani's departure after 14 years
blurb: Also passed a Food Security Grant Program ordinance, an ambulance debt write-off policy, and funding for Riverwalk North design work.

title: State of the Schools: special-education enrollment climbs to a county-high 27%
blurb: Also: the FY27 budget calendar is set, the 2026-27 school calendar drops its staggered kindergarten start, and Lancia reports meeting with Governor Mills on school funding.

title: Finance Subcommittee opens budget season with a 9.88% proposed increase
blurb: Also: the district's energy-efficiency project already outperforms its $255,000 savings guarantee, and a new Pre-K program takes shape.

title: Planning Board approves Prompto Oil Change site plan, previews Redeemer Church relocation
blurb: Also approved updated child-care ordinance language; no votes were contested.

title: Council hears FY2025 audit's clean opinion, caught in a Bucket Brigade dispute
blurb: Nine residents spoke about a dispute between the Westbrook Bucket Brigade and the Historical Society's leadership, while routine capital and school funding items advanced.

title: Council remembers former Councilor John O'Hara, advances FY26 Capital Improvement Plan
blurb: Firefighters urged the Council to restore funding for a regional fire training facility, and the plan included nearly $2 million in new general obligation bonds.

title: FY25 audit comes back clean as the district launches its own Pre-K program
blurb: Also: a bond-fund reallocation request heads to City Council and six School Department policies pass in one vote.

title: Planning Board approves early tree-clearing phase for Buddhist temple project
blurb: The board also elected 2026 officers and previewed a warehouse addition and new child-care ordinance language.

title: Council previews a PFAS testing agreement with GPCOG
blurb: Also: two new liquor licenses approved, a personal-property-tax outreach program announced, and CDBG grant applications advanced.

title: Committee of the Whole leaves remote-participation policy unchanged
blurb: A short, single-item workshop session with no public comment; the board took no further action on the referral.

title: Westbrook's halal-certified meals program expands districtwide as subcommittee assignments are set for the year
blurb: Also: a new WRVC recruiting video debuts and the committee closes with a personnel matter in executive session.

title: Rifle suppressor purchase for police passes 6–1 after sharp debate
blurb: The Council also heard an early PFAS update on three city-owned parcels and confirmed election clerks and a Zoning Board of Appeals alternate.
hotNote: Suppressor purchase, 6–1 split (Munro) + forceful public debate

title: Foster Street parking dispute splits Council 5–1
blurb: Also: a big win on next year's workers' comp costs, a Town Line Diner liquor license, and a trash-collection problem flagged by a resident.
hotNote: Foster St. parking, 5–1 split (Rairdon)
